data.description:
Scope: root-level `src/rebar/*.py` plus `attest/`, `metrics/`, `review_bot/`, `opcert_service/`, `audit/`, `grounding/`, `_guides/`. ~180 lines leave of 7,248 comment lines (2.5%) — this scope is in good health and the yield is concentrated, not diffuse.

SURFACED A LIVE DEFECT, filed separately: `_mcp_models.BridgeFsckOut` omits `binding_drift`, so the MCP outputSchema under-declares a field `bridge_fsck.py:217` always returns. The comment at `_mcp_models.py:31-34` claiming 'the cross-interface schema tests pin both to the canonical schema' is FALSE — those model names appear zero times in tests/. That false assurance is why the drift went unnoticed.

Two prior leads resolved AGAINST the hypothesis and belong in do_not_move: `_mcp_llm.py`'s 121 docstring lines are the literal wire-visible MCP tool descriptions FastMCP publishes to clients — API surface, not narration, zero recoverable. And `_config_schema.py`'s `# read-via:` markers are machine-consumed by `scripts/check_config_reads.py`, a CI gate — deleting one breaks CI.

Caveat that bounds this shard: 280 of `_config_schema.py`'s 792 lines are comments, and for many keys they are the ONLY documentation — `docs/config.md` has zero coverage for `completion_floor_active`, `comment_max_chars`, `auth_proxy_secret_env`. Recovering more than ~34 lines there requires writing those doc rows FIRST, or the trim destroys documentation rather than relocating it.

Three new ADRs proposed from `review_bot/`: bounded shutdown (drain/cancel/grace-period chain, test-pinned against docker-compose `stop_grace_period`); the deploy-safe in-flight counter and its deliberate over-count; retryable coverage gaps deferring vote-less under a bounded budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination
- [ ] The shard's do_not_move list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` BEFORE any edit lands
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only where obsolete
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost
data.title: Comment triage: root modules and services
